_meta.purpose: Soil type reference used by the soil evidence-fusion module (app/services/soil.py) and by the crop suitability scorer (app/services/suitability.py).

id.note: The Indian soil names in the locale files (enum.soil_type.*) follow the standard NBSS&LUP / ICAR classification used across Maharashtra.

texture_class.method: Coarse heavy/medium/light grouping, using the same vocabulary EcoCrop publishes, assigned from the standard classification of each soil. Black cotton soil is a vertisol (heavy); red and laterite soils are light-to-medium; sandy loam is light.
texture_class.review_needed: A soil scientist should confirm the seven assignments before any field pilot.

ecocrop_drainage.method: Expresses each soil in EcoCrop's drainage vocabulary so it can be compared against EcoCrop's per-crop drainage requirement. Black and clay-loam soils are recorded as 'well (dry spells)' rather than 'poorly drained' because vertisols crack and dry out in summer (see cracks_in_summer) - they are impermeable, not waterlogged. That distinction is exactly the one that previously made this table call black soil a poor choice for cotton.
ecocrop_drainage.review_needed: Confirm before any field pilot, in particular for SALINE.

water_retention.note: Qualitative, descriptive only. No scoring rule reads this field any more; crop/soil matching is driven by the EcoCrop-derived texture and drainage vocabulary.

drainage.note: Qualitative, descriptive only - see ecocrop_drainage for the field the matcher uses.

rain_behaviour_likelihood.note: OUR OWN ESTIMATES for the fusion algorithm. Not published values, not calibrated against any labelled dataset. Values are relative weights; app/services/crops.py:water_behaviour_distribution normalises them into a distribution, so they do not need to sum to 1.0 here.
rain_behaviour_likelihood.todo_before_field_pilot: Calibrate against real farmer-observation plus soil-test pairs. Until then the fused confidence is a relative indicator only.

typical_crops.note: Removed in schema 2. It used to be a hand-written list. It is now derived by inverting the sourced crop/soil match in app/services/crops.py:typical_crops_for_soil, so the two tables cannot drift apart.

fields.id: stable code, matches soil_type codes used across the app and the locale keys enum.soil_type.<CODE>
fields.rain_behaviour_likelihood: RELATIVE likelihood that a farmer reporting this rain behaviour actually has this soil
